name: Ravenfield
headline: The Brighton Housing Authority is building Ravenfield Senior Apartments, 46 income-restricted homes for adults 62+ at 30% to 60% AMI (11 with project-based vouchers) at 590 S. 27th Ave. in Brighton, after winning 2025 Round One federal 9% and state credits from CHFA.
why_it_matters: A small housing authority acting as its own developer for the first time brought a 9% senior deal from site purchase to groundbreaking in about two and a half years. It used a county ARPA-backed land loan, its own vouchers and seller note, and the city's first water fee-in-lieu for affordable housing.

status.label: Under construction (groundbreaking reported 2026-05-27); completion expected 2027
status.detail: The Brighton Blade reported the groundbreaking ceremony on 2026-05-27. BHA's director cited a roughly 15-month build, finishing around the middle of 2027; the article's headline says fall 2027. No public building permit or financing closing record was found.

next_step: Watch for BHA leasing and waitlist announcements on the project website and a certificate of occupancy in mid-to-late 2027.

background.text: BHA bought the site from the adjacent church, which ran a competitive sale meant to secure a use that benefits the community. The purchase was financed through an Adams County program using ARPA funds. The price is not public.

BHA says it spent over $30,000 on neighbor outreach, and that neighborhood opposition was not a factor in the rezoning. The design came from a charrette with city and county leaders and focus groups with BHA senior residents.

BHA owns all of Brighton's senior LIHTC housing (all but 20 of the 213 comparable units in the market area). At the time of the market study only 4 were vacant, with a combined waitlist of 423 senior households.
This is BHA's third affordable senior community in Brighton, after Libretto and Brighton Village, and a pivotal project in building BHA's capacity to act as its own developer.
A City Council member said a second phase on the same property is being considered, probably another building with about double the capacity.
BHA services will include Food Bank of the Rockies food delivery, RTD and ARC thrift store vouchers, resource fairs and clothing drives, and links to the Eagle View Adult Center.

Amenities: first-floor library with fireplace, large kitchen and dining room, a pocket amenity space on each floor, a rooftop patio, a community mud room with bike storage, raised garden beds, a fire pit and a walking path around the site. Units have in-unit washers and dryers, and upper units have Juliet balconies.
The design team says rounds of redesign saved over $500,000; two elevators and local permit, tap and impact fees push costs up.
